topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: The Biological and Genetic Nature of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core nature of cancer as a micro-evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous cellular processes, microenvironmental factors, and mutation accumulation.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how external exposures, the debate over intrinsic versus environmental risks, and global epidemiological variations demonstrate the impact of external factors on cancer incidence.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis through immune disruption and chronic inflammation, highlighted by the case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which environmental, dietary, and physical agents undergo metabolic conversion to induce DNA damage and mutagenic adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Tissue Context, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, tissue specificity, and host developmental timing provide the permissive conditions required for tumor development.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational signatures and determine carcinogenic risk.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Carcinogenic Risk-Benefit Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a summary of environmental cancer causation and reflections on evaluating everyday exposure risks against practical benefits.
